name: checkstyle
description: Checkstyle is a development tool to help programmers write Java code that adheres to a coding standard. By default it supports the Google Java Style Guide and Sun Code Conventions, but is highly configurable. It can be invoked with an ANT task and a command line program.
one_liner: A tool that automatically checks Java code against a company's coding style rules.
buyer: No new buyer here — this is decades-old, free, and already embedded in most Java teams' CI pipelines.
business_use_cases: A Java engineering team runs it automatically in CI to block pull requests that violate style rules.
A consultancy sets it up as part of a broader "code quality baseline" engagement for a client's legacy Java codebase.

money_ideas.idea: Wrap it into a hosted "code quality dashboard" for enterprise Java teams as one signal among several.

steal_this: Not a weekend opportunity — it's mature, free, and the market for standalone style-linting products has already been won by free tooling.
